Introduction

In this project, we will be analysing the demand for rented bikes in Seoul, with the aims of predicting the demand for rented bikes in Seoul considering time and weather variables. This predictive model will be useful for helping to mainting a stable supply for bike renters, as well as help rented bike companies to project revenues in the future.

Data

Raw Dataset

The Seoul rented bikes data set has 8760 observations across 13 features. Each observation records details of the date, hourly bike demand, hour of day, temperature, rainfall, snowfall and other time and weather related-variables.

Cleaning

In the raw data set, a variable called functioning_day was used to signify if the bike-renting system was operational or not. We realised that when functioning_day == “no,” all instances of rented_bike_count had a value of 0. As we are interested in the number of rented bikes, this would not be relevant for our goal.

We also used clean_names() to ensure that all variables have in snake_case for simplicity when writing code.

Feature Engineering

We ultimately engineered four variables, but one of which will not be used in our linear model, which will be explained in later sections of this report.

hour_holiday — factor that matches an hour of day to whether that day is a holiday or not.

precipitation — has values 1 or 0, used to indicate if there was any forms of rainfall or snowfall.

is_weekend — determines if the day is a weekday or during the weekend.

peak — determines if the hour of day is a peak commuting time. We have defined this to be 7-9am and 5-7pm. This is the engineered variable that will be removed after exploratory data analysis (EDA).

Key Predictors

For our model the following variables are what we will consider: rented_bike_count, hour_holiday, is_weekend, temperature_c, humidity_percent, seasons and precipitation.

Below is a variable table of the clean data:

Variable Name Type Description
rented_bike_count numerical number of bikes rented per hour
hour_holiday categorical describes the hour of day, and whether the day is a holiday or not
is_weekend categorical determines if it is a day in the week or in the weekend
temperature_c numerical temperature of Seoul in degrees Celsius
humidity_percent numerical humidity of Seoul in percent
seasons categorical determines if the day is in winter, spring, summer or autumn
precipitation numerical has values 1 or 0 used to determine if there was any precipitation during the hour of day

Splitting Dataset and Building Workflow

##  7 hour_holiday_X2_Holiday   -99.7    160.       -0.623 5.33e-  1
##  8 hour_holiday_X3_Holiday  -260.     155.       -1.69  9.20e-  2
##  9 hour_holiday_X4_Holiday  -425.     172.       -2.48  1.33e-  2
## 10 hour_holiday_X5_Holiday  -410.     155.       -2.65  8.00e-  3
## # ℹ 45 more rows

Notice our Linear model has 55 terms including the baseline. This is caused by the factoring by combining the original variables hour and holiday together.

Below is the expression of our linear model:

\[ \begin{aligned} \widehat{\text{rented bike count}} &= 903.26 - 68.74 \times \text{is weekend} + 20.38 \times \text{temperature c} - 6.70 \times \text{humidity percent} \\ &\quad - 247.01 \times \text{precipitation} - 80.61 \times \text{hour holiday X1 Holiday} - 99.72 \times \text{hour holiday X2 Holiday} + \dots \\ &\quad - 29.98 \times \text{hour holiday X0 No.Holiday} - 132.89 \times \text{hour holiday X1 No.Holiday} + \dots \\ &\quad - 66.15 \times \text{seasons Spring} + 11.12 \times \text{seasons Summer} - 283.33 \times \text{seasons Winter} \end{aligned} \] Notice that ‘seasons_Autumn’ does not have its own term. This is because the variable has been in a sense absorbed into the baseline.

Variables are also not in snake_case as latex in RMarkdown provides an output that is not clean.
